vrcc_travel_policy_v1.pdf.text: VRCC Consortium Travel Policy Document Version 1.0 (Effective 2024). Section 1: Per Diem and Meals. Employees traveling on official VRCC business are entitled to a maximum daily meal per diem of $65 per day. Any meal expenditure exceeding $65 per day requires pre-authorization by the regional comptroller. Section 2: Lodging Allowances. The standard hotel nightly rate ceiling is fixed at $180 per night for domestic travel and $220 for international travel. Room service and minibar charges are strictly non-reimbursable under Policy 1.0. Section 3: Discretionary Spending. The discretionary project spending cap without executive review is $2,500 per trip. All receipts must be submitted to expense-audit@vaelen.internal within 14 calendar days.

vrcc_travel_policy_v2.pdf.text: VRCC Consortium Travel Policy Document Version 2.4 (Effective January 2026). Notice: This policy explicitly supersedes Version 1.0 in its entirety. Section 1: Per Diem and Subsistence. Under Policy Version 2.4, the updated daily meal per diem allowance is raised to exactly $92 per day. Breakfast is allocated $22, lunch $28, and dinner $42. Alcohol remains non-reimbursable. Section 2: Lodging Ceilings. The updated standard hotel ceiling is increased to $245 per night for all standard domestic tier-1 cities. For Tier-2 cities, the cap is $195 per night.

Section 3: Executive Approval Thresholds. Discretionary travel spending authority is expanded: project directors can approve expenses up to $4,000 per trip. Expenses exceeding $4,000 require written clearance from Chief Financial Officer Marcus Vance. Section 4: Mileage and Electric Fleet. Employees driving company electric vehicles receive a charging stipend of $0.34 per mile. Car rental upgrades to premium tier require Medical Disability Form MED-7.

aethelgard_titan_drone_specs.pdf.text: Aethelgard Dynamics - Titan-X Heavy Autonomous Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Specifications. 1. Propulsion and Battery Core: The Titan-X is powered by an advanced Lithium-Sulfur solid-core battery pack with an energy density of 420 Wh/kg. The battery system operates at a nominal bus voltage of 74.0 Volts and delivers 85 Amp-hours. Rotor architecture utilizes an octocopter coaxial-tilt layout with carbon-fiber reinforced blades.

2. Payload Capacity and Aerodynamics: The maximum certified payload capacity of the Titan-X is exactly 18.4 kilograms. Total maximum takeoff weight (MTOW) is 46.8 kilograms. Under standard sea-level atmospheric conditions (ISA), the maximum continuous flight endurance is 142 minutes with a 5 kg sensor payload.

3. Avionics and Communication Protocol: Primary telemetry is maintained via the proprietary Kestrel-Link 900 MHz redundant datalink with AES-256-GCM encryption. Operational ceiling is restricted to 4,500 meters above ground level. In the event of lost telemetry exceeding 45 seconds, the emergency return-to-base sequence RTB-ALPHA is automatically engaged.

zephyros_avionics_handbook.pdf.text: Zephyros Aerospace Avionics Systems Engineering Manual ? Chapter 1. Subsection 1.1: Technical Diagnostics for Module ZX-1017. The primary telemetry carrier frequency for subsystem 1 is calibrated to 120.45 MHz. During nominal sub-orbital transit, coolant flow rate must be maintained at 11.5 liters per minute. The safety interlock threshold for voltage regulator VREG-1 is set at 24.1 V. Subsection 1.2: Standard Operating Procedure. Inspect pressure seal GASKET-1 every 250 operating cycles. If differential pressure drops below 1.25 bar, issue alarm CODE-1017-WARN and isolate the purge valve.
